title: Effects of Casein Hydrolysate Ingestion on Thermoregulatory Responses in Healthy Adults during Exercise in Heated Conditions: A Randomized Crossover Trial

what_it_measured.text: We investigated the effects of casein hydrolysate ingestion on thermoregulatory responses during exercise in the heat.
Then, we investigated the effect of CH ingestion on thermoregulatory responses and exercise tolerance under heated conditions (main experiment).

dose.text: In a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover trial, five men and five women consumed either 5 g of casein hydrolysate or placebo.

route.text: In a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover trial, five men and five women consumed either 5 g of casein hydrolysate or placebo.

endpoint.text: Changes in the primary outcomes (i.e., Tco, Tsk, and sweat rate) from their BL values (∆) were calculated during exercise in the main experiment.
Local sweat rate was measured continuously using the ventilated capsule method.
The relationship between ∆sweat rate and ∆TAA was evaluated using the Pearson’s correlation test.

reported_results.text: Exercise time to exhaustion, body core temperature, forearm sweat rate, and forearm cutaneous vascular conductance did not differ different between the conditions. However, chest sweat rate and mean skin temperature increased upon casein hydrolysate ingestion compared with placebo during exercise.
